newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Reports of CVRD gold find stump market.
newsitem.headline: Reports of CVRD gold find stump market.

text.p: Reports that state mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce found major new gold and copper deposits in northern Brazil have baffled investors, leaving them unsure whether to buy or sell, analysts said.
CVRD shares, which surged Tuesday on a local newspaper report of an "historic" CVRD gold-copper discovery in Para state, posted further gains Wednesday despite company denials.
"There is definitely confusion out there," said Gilberto Tannovschi, a trader at Banco Antonio de Queiroz.
Felipe Zaghan, a mining analyst with Indosuez Capital, said stock investors, upbeat on the promise of a major new gold deposit, have merely been speculating on CVRD shares.
Be he added: "There is no reason at this point for the price to go up."
Company officials reiterated Wednesday that they do not have any technical data to support O Estado do S. Paulo reports that rich new gold and copper deposits have been found in the Carajas area.
"There are indications but we cannot quantify anything," a company spokesman said.
Drilling in the Igarape-Bahia region revealed "promising" gold and copper mineralization but it is much too early to say if the exploration targets are major discoveries, he said.

Analysts said stock investors chose to focus on the positive, ignoring the chance that any new deposit could prompt an upward revaluation of CVRD or stall the firm's privatization, set to begin in 1997's first quarter, they said.
They added that CVRD's privatization is likely to be a sensitive political issue and a new discovery might result in calls by government opponents for delays and more studies before any sale.

"If there is something big, the company's value will really go up," said one analyst, who added the Estado reports were the third "exaggerated" report of a CVRD find since the government announced its plans to privatize the firm.
"There's too much uncertainty," the analyst said. "Everytime a bombastic article like this comes out, it confuses the market."
